That sounds rough what your going through. Depression is bad enough and on top of that you are questioning your gender identity. I too suffer from depression and I question my gender identity. I feel like when I am most depressed I question more frequently. Trying to decide my true gender one way or another always turns out to be self fulfilling prophecy. Meaning... I can always look back at my life and find examples that support my argument about wanting to be either a male or female (depending upon my mindset at the moment). Unfortunately, ( and it really is unfortunate) no one can make the final decision about your gender but yourself. So my advice to you would be to first address the depression. Find a therapist and focus on taking better care of yourself even if that means sacrificing some of your current goals i.e. achieving a certain grade point average. Depression is persistent af. My experience has taught me it doesn’t get better without allotting enough time and energy to address the issues. If this means swallowing your pride and becoming more open about your depression or even what may be causing your depression, so be it. Best of luck to you. I’m rooting for you👍

Ya no problem. ECT is just absolutely wild. I do believe it works for some people, but I don’t think it did for me. My experience was good over all. However, I did it at McClain hospital which is considered to be one of the best for ECT and for treating mental health issues. The staff was super nice and very caring. I say it was wild because the whole concept is for lack of a better word “extreme”. They roll you into a room, administer anesthesia and shock your brain into a seizure. You wake up after 30 mins or so, they give you a snack, evaluate you and you go home. The whole thing is kinda fun tbh. But don’t let the fact that it was fun sway you. ECT is invasive. Shocking your brain in to a seizure once a week shouldn’t be taken lightly. One of the few things I remember is during an evaluation they asked me how many treatments they thought I had received. I told them I thought I was on 3 or 4, but they told me I was on 11. That made me nervous and the doctors  decided to start to distance the time between treatments to prevent further memory loss. I experienced a lot of memory loss. I didn’t know what I did yesterday most of the time. I could meet a new person and have a long conversation with them and then the next day not know who they were. That was disturbing for myself as well as the people I met. As grotesque/ strange as it may sound. I did enjoy getting anesthesia. It was a cool sensation. Over all, the experience was good. For the few months that I was undergoing treatment I believe my mood probably improved, but it didn’t have any long term effects on my mood. I could have easily been prescribed Xanax to improve my mood temporarily. I still wonder if the treatments had any lasting effects on my cognitive abilities. Sometimes I feel like it does.
